_source: L19 (work plan 2). More of the original's voice, never contradicting it and never a floor count. Built on its own phrases: the Chief's Hall inscription (MEASURE THE GRAIN. COUNT THE FLASKS. KEEP THE DOOR.), the architect and his toys, the bell with no clapper, the scar that misfires every spell, the dungeon still being built. Budget (origins.json): one 'tell' per delve, on its first floor.

tomb: The dead here were laid out in rows, and the rows were counted.
Every niche has a name scratched out of it.
The names were chiselled, then chiselled out - somebody wanted them forgotten twice.
Grave goods, left where they lay. Nobody down here needs a comb.
A tomb cut for one, filled by a hundred.
The lids are heavy, and some have been moved from the inside.
mine: Someone dug here for something, and stopped all at once.
The seam glitters where the scar has been at it.
The pick-marks run straight a while, then wander like the digger did.
A cart sits full on a track that ends in solid rock.
They were following something down. It was following them.
There is ore-light here, where there should be none.
fortress: Arrow-slits face inward. Whoever held this was keeping something in.
The gate was barred from the far side.
Murder-holes over the only door - somebody expected guests.
The walls are thick enough to keep a siege out, or a thing in.
A standard still hangs over the hall, too rotted to read.
The well in the yard is capped with iron and chained.
temple: The altar is clean. Nobody down here cleans.
Prayers are carved low on the walls, where a kneeling hand would reach.
Candles burnt to stubs, and relit since. By whom?
The font holds water that should have dried an age ago.
One god's name on the lintel, scratched over with another's.
Someone still leaves bread on the step.
lair: The floor is worn smooth by something heavy that came and went.
It smells of old fur and new blood.
Bones cracked for the marrow, and stacked with care.
The nest is still warm. Mind that.
Claw-marks climb the wall and stop flat against the ceiling.
Something counted the exits here before you did.
prison: The cells lock from the outside, and some are still locked.
Tally marks, thousands of them, and then none.
A key-ring on a dead gaoler, and every cell still shut.
Names and dates on the walls, then dates with no names.
The last cell is swept clean, and its door stands open.
Scratches on the inside of the doors. All of them.
works: Benches, tools, a half-made thing nobody finished. Don't touch the architect's toys.
The work stopped mid-stroke, as if called away.
Half a machine, and no telling what the other half was for.
Chalk sums cover the wall - the same sum, wrong every time.
The architect's bench is set for a hand that never came back.
Tools laid out for a job nobody named. Leave the architect's toys be.
warren: Doorways, chimneys, a street sign - a whole town, swallowed.
Somebody lived here once and kept a window box.
A doorway in the floor, and a doorway in the ceiling right above it.
Washing on a line, gone to dust, still pegged.
A whole street, folded into the dark like a letter.
A doll in a window box. Someone waved from here, once.

descend: %s %s down past the guild post. The door is kept behind them.
%s %s into the dark below Bellmire, counting the flasks.
%s %s below, where the lamps are lit against nothing good.
%s %s down the guild stair, flasks stowed and counted.
%s %s into the dark - light first, steel after.
%s %s below Bellmire, where the meadow turns to mountain.
%s %s past the memorial and down into the deep.
%s %s on the guild's coin, and the guild wants a return.
%s %s below, boots loud on the first stair and quiet after.
%s %s into the scar with the lamps trimmed low.
%s %s down, and Bellmire holds its breath.
%s %s below with the guild's coin and the guild's warning.
%s %s down the scar while the crier is still reading the name.
%s %s into the deep, and the memorial gets another look on the way past.
%s %s below, lamp trimmed, flasks counted, door kept behind them.
%s %s down where the mountain starts under the meadow.
%s %s into the scar, and the dark makes room.
cleared: Floor %d is done, and the guild writes it down.
Floor %d - the dark backs off a step.
Floor %d quiets, and something deeper takes notice.
Floor %d won. Count the flasks; one is always short.
Floor %d cleared; the lamps move down a step.
Floor %d is still, and the Chronicle catches up.
Floor %d holds. The scar keeps count too.
Floor %d gives it up. The lamps go lower.
Floor %d cleared - the guild owes nothing yet.
Floor %d empty, and the quiet is the suspicious kind.
Floor %d is behind them. So is the way out.
Floor %d settled. Something below shifts its weight.
Floor %d cleared, and the Chronicle spells the name right.

lord_intros.hollow_king: The braziers in the hall burn blue, and then burn cold.
lord_intros.grubmother: The floor is wet, and getting wetter.
lord_intros.rattling_host: Somewhere ahead, something counts its own bones out loud.
lord_intros.nightwing: Every torch on the floor gutters at once.
lord_intros.gravewyrm: The dungeon was built around this, and it knows it.
lord_intros.ossuary_lord: It has waited a very long time. A little longer is nothing.
lord_intros.pale_duchess: A lady laughs somewhere ahead, very politely.
lord_intros.mourncoil: Breath steams. Then the steam freezes.

unique_intros.mother_silk: The threads across the doorway are new.
unique_intros.weeping_bowman: A string twangs in the dark, and something weeps after it.
unique_intros.cinderjack: Someone has been playing with the firepits.
unique_intros.kept: A voice the guild knew calls a name the guild remembers.

misfire: That wasn't the spell I cast.
Not my spell. Not my fault.
%s's %s goes wrong - the scar answers (%d vs DC %d).
%s reaches for %s and the scar hands back something else (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s comes out sideways - wild magic (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s turns in their hand - the scar answers (%d vs DC %d).
%s tries %s and the ground gives it back wrong (%d vs DC %d).
%s's %s unravels mid-word - wild magic (%d vs DC %d).
%s casts %s; the scar casts something else (%d vs DC %d).
epitaphs: Measured the grain. Counted the flasks. Kept the door.
The scar keeps what it takes.
Went down with a lamp. Did not come up.
The guild writes the name and keeps it.
Somewhere below, a bell with no clapper rings once.
One floor too many.
Lit a lamp. The dark kept it.
Counted every flask but the last.
The guild writes the name; the scar keeps the rest.
Measured the grain. The grain ran out.
Went down proving something. Proved it.
Kept the door, until the door kept them.
The bell with no clapper rang, and they did not come up.
Named on the roll, and marked with a dagger.
Paid the guild's price in full.
The door held. They did not.
Last seen going down, lamp high.
The Chronicle spells the name right, at least.
Fed the scar and asked for nothing.
A good hand with a flask, to the end.
Kept the door one floor too long.
Took the stair down and the guild's coin with it.
Knew the shapes. Met a new one.
Walked in light, left in the dark.
The lamp came back. They did not.
Marked present on the roll, and absent everywhere else.
Trimmed the lamp low to save oil. Saved oil.
Bellmire remembers the name and nothing else.
Went down for the gold and found the rest of it.
Mended everyone but themselves.
The flask was full. The hand was slow.
Stood where the floor lied.
No body to bury. The guild buried the name.

forge.1: Bellmire iron: honest, dull, and better than bare hands.
forge.2: Folded twice; the smith signs it.
forge.3: Runes along the fuller smoulder when it is drawn.
forge.4: Dragontooth - nobody in Bellmire will say whose tooth.
forge.5: Scarforged. It hums when the dark is near.

town_levels_for_the_desktop._note: For the desktop's town.gd if it wants them (the laptop does not edit town.gd): an announcement when Bellmire reaches a level, in the original's voice.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.1: Bellmire is a hamlet with a hole in it.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.2: Bellmire is a village now. The guild post has a door.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.3: Bellmire stands as a market town. Measure the grain.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.4: Bellmire grows into a town of note. Count the flasks.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.5: Bellmire is a walled town. Keep the door.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.6: Bellmire is a city in all but charter.
town_levels_for_the_desktop.7: Bellmire is a city. The scar is still deeper than it was.

e3po._note: E3PO - Commander of the Guards. He CANNOT die; badly hurt he withdraws to the barracks, heals, and returns. Immortal, beloved, a little pompous, utterly reliable. For the desktop's raids.gd/town.gd if it wires him (content worker never touches code). Additive; dead until wired.
intro: E3PO takes the wall. The whole guard stands straighter.
The Commander is on the field. Nobody tells him to be careful.
The gate opens, and it is only E3PO coming out to meet them.
E3PO arrives at a walk. Running would suggest doubt.
The Commander's voice reaches the back of the square before he does.
withdraw: E3PO is hauled to the barracks, swearing he is fine.
The Commander falls back to heal. He will be back before you miss him.
Too much even for E3PO - he withdraws to the barracks.
They carry E3PO off the wall. 'A scratch,' he says, bleeding freely.
E3PO goes down on one knee and the whole wall goes quiet. Then he swears, and it starts breathing again.
The Commander is carried off still giving orders over a shoulder.
'Barracks. Briefly.' E3PO lets himself be helped, which costs him more than the wound.
return: E3PO is back on the wall, mended and mortified.
The Commander returns to duty. He apologises to no one.
E3PO retakes the gate, good as new and twice as loud.
E3PO walks out of the barracks buckling the last strap. 'Where were we.'
The Commander returns with fresh bandages and the same volume.
E3PO is back, and the raiders can tell from the far field.
says: Hold the line. The line holds because I say so.
I have died exactly never. Let us keep the record.
Measure the grain, count the flasks, and leave the gate to me.
A guard who runs is a guard I must replace, and I hate paperwork.
They do not pay me to fall. They do not pay me at all - I simply refuse to leave.
The door stays shut. That is the whole job, and I am very good at it.
Bellmire sleeps because I do not.
Shapes, not numbers. That goes for raiders too.
I do not require a monument. A kept door will do.
If the gate holds and the grain is counted, the day is a success. The rest is weather.
Call me Commander. 'Sir' is for men who might retire.
town_talk: They say E3PO has held the gate since before there was a gate.
Old-timers swear E3PO has outlived three of his own gravestones.
The children drill with sticks and name the loudest one E3PO.
No raider has taken the Keep door while the Commander draws breath - which is to say, never.
The guild keeps a chair for E3PO at every feast. He never sits; he watches the door.
The Watch say the Commander's armour has more dents than the gate has nails.
There is a standing wager at the tavern on what could fell E3PO. Nobody has collected.
The masons built the new wall a hand taller because he asked twice.
They tried to carve him a statue. He made them turn it to face the door.
Every recruit hears the same first words: 'The door stays shut.'
e3po._note_extras: Added keys (C-cycle 5): raid / disaster / festival lines, and viewer_roll keyed by outcome (crit, high, low, fumble) for the d20. Same voice as 'says'. Additive; dead until wired.
raid: E3PO plants himself in the gateway. 'This far. No further, and I am being generous.'
The Commander walks the wall at a stroll, which is somehow worse for the raiders.
'Form up on me! I am the easiest thing on this field to find.'
E3PO takes a blow meant for a bowman, then tells the bowman off for standing there.
'They brought ladders. Charming. Fetch the poles.'
The Commander counts the raiders aloud. The guard find it steadying. The raiders do not.
'Nobody dies tonight on my watch. I have written it down, so it is official.'
E3PO shoulders the gate shut with a raider still arguing on the other side.
disaster: E3PO has the bucket line running before anyone thinks to ask him.
'Fire does not negotiate. Neither do I. Pass the buckets.'
The Commander carries two children out of the smoke and apologises for the noise.
'A disaster is a raid with worse manners. Work the problem.'
E3PO stands in the floodwater directing carts, soaked to the breastplate.
'Grain to the Keep, flasks to the chapel, people first. Move.'
The Commander does not sleep while the town is burning, drowning or shaking.
'Count the living twice. Then count them again for me.'
festival: E3PO attends the feast in full harness and declines a chair, as always.
'Dance. Someone has to watch the door while you do.'
The Commander judges the pie contest and refuses to be bribed, loudly, for an hour.
E3PO is talked into one dance and performs it like a drill.
'Festival rules: drink what you like. The gate stays shut.'
They hand the Commander a flower crown. He wears it over the helm.
E3PO lifts a cup to the dead, names every one, and goes back to the wall.

crit: 'Now THAT is how it is done. Write it down. Write it twice.'
The Commander salutes. From E3PO, that is a parade.
'Were you trained by me? No? Then you are frighteningly talented.'
high: The Commander nods once. The guild post treats it as a medal.
low: 'Luck is a resource and you have spent yours. Use skill.'
The Commander looks away politely, which is worse than shouting.
'We will say the dice were tired.'
fumble: 'I have seen worse. I have not seen worse today.'
The Commander writes something in his book. It is not your name spelled kindly.
'Stand up. Dust off. The dice do not get the last word. I do.'

town_life._note: Ambient Bellmire flavour as the town grows - crier calls, market and guild chatter, building news. For the desktop's town.gd if it wires a ticker; content worker never touches code. Additive; dead until wired.
crier: Grain measured, flasks counted, door kept - Bellmire stands another day!
Fresh off the river: trout, and a tale with every one.
The guild takes names at the post. Bring your own courage.
Lamps lit, walls walked, all's well - or well enough.
Another delver down the scar. Put a copper on them coming back up.
market: Two coppers the carp, and the carp is grinning.
Dye by the ounce - name a colour, Bellmire keeps it now.
Scarglass! Cheap, and only slightly cursed!
Boots that have walked further than you have, half off.
growth: The masons raised a new course on the wall today.
A second well dug, and the queue at the first one shorter.
They are building where the fields used to stop.
The guild post has two doors now. Both kept.

propositions._note: Viewer-voting town laws (T4). 17 across law/taxes/militia/building/faith/outsiders. Each names a CONSEQUENCE, good and bad - a law that only helps is boring. Readable at a glance. Dead until wired.

entries.title: The Gallows Law
entries.flavour: Thieves hang, not fine. The guild says it will clear the market of cutpurses.
entries.good: Crime falls; the market feels safe to spend in.
entries.bad: The desperate turn to worse than theft, and some good hands leave town.

entries.title: Trial by the Roll
entries.flavour: Let the accused delve the scar. Come back up, and you walk free.
entries.good: Wildly popular on stream, and the dungeon runs hot.
entries.bad: The innocent die below, and the guild loses good names.

entries.title: Debtors' Pardon
entries.flavour: Wipe the slate. Come spring, no one in Bellmire owes a copper.
entries.good: The poor breathe again; loyalty climbs.
entries.bad: The lenders shut their purses, and coin stops moving.

entries.title: Raise the Grain Tithe
entries.flavour: A heavier cut of every harvest goes to the town coffers.
entries.good: The treasury swells; walls and wages get paid.
entries.bad: Full barns, thin bellies - the folk grumble, and some go hungry.

entries.title: The Free Market Charter
entries.flavour: Drop the market tolls. Any trader sells in Bellmire toll-free.
entries.good: Caravans flock in; the stalls overflow.
entries.bad: The coffers thin, and the guild's grip slips.

entries.title: Toll at the Ford
entries.flavour: A copper to cross, paid to the Ferryman, paid to the town.
entries.bad: Traders grumble, some ford downstream, and the Ferryman is not thanked.

entries.title: Raise the Militia Levy
entries.flavour: Every household sends a hand to the wall.
entries.good: The guard doubles; raiders think twice.
entries.bad: Fewer hands in the fields - the town is safer but poorer.

entries.title: Arm the Delvers
entries.flavour: Guild steel for anyone who will hold the gate.
entries.bad: Armed and idle men make their own trouble.

entries.title: Night Curfew
entries.flavour: Lamps out, doors barred, the Watch walks till dawn.
entries.good: No raid slips in by night.
entries.bad: The taverns empty; the folk feel watched, not kept.

entries.title: Wall the Town
entries.flavour: Stone where the fields stop. The masons are ready and waiting.
entries.bad: It costs a fortune, and the harvest waits while the masons build.

entries.title: Dig the Second Well
entries.flavour: One well, long queues, and the dry months coming.
entries.good: Water for all, even in a drought.
entries.bad: The diggers want paying, and they keep hitting scarstone.

entries.title: Pave the Market Square
entries.flavour: Mud to flagstone, fit for a city.
entries.good: Traders linger; the town looks the part.
entries.bad: A whole season's coin, sunk into the ground.

entries.title: Ring the Festival
entries.flavour: A feast day on the guild's coin, and the clapperless bell rung anyway.
entries.good: Spirits soar; both loyalty and trade rise.
entries.bad: A day's work lost, and a day's coin with it.

entries.title: Tithe to the Chapel
entries.flavour: Fund the temple and light every candle.
entries.good: The faithful are glad; the sick are tended.
entries.bad: Coin the walls could have used.

entries.title: Open the Gates to Refugees
entries.flavour: Folk fleeing the scar-lands crowd the Ford by the hundred.
entries.good: New hands for the fields and the wall.
entries.bad: More mouths to feed - and sickness travels with them.

entries.title: Hire the Sellswords
entries.flavour: Coin for blades that answer to gold, not the guild.
entries.good: Hard muscle for the hard floors.
entries.bad: They stay bought only as long as you keep paying.

entries.title: Shut the Border
entries.flavour: No stranger past the Ford without the guild's word.
entries.good: No raider walks in wearing a traveller's coat.
entries.bad: Trade withers, and the town turns inward and small.

disasters._note: Natural disasters (D34). For each: begin (Chronicle line), during (lines while it lasts), pass (line when it ends), cost (plain statement of what it should cost the town, for the desktop to implement). Dead until wired.

volcano.begin: The mountain above the scar wakes - ash on the wind, and the sky goes copper.
during: Ash falls on Bellmire; the sun is a dull coin behind the smoke.
The river runs grey, and the fish float up dead.
Cinders tick off the roof-tiles all night; nobody opens a shutter.
The crier reads the day's news through a cloth over his mouth.
volcano.pass: The mountain settles. Ash greys every roof, but the air clears.
volcano.cost: A buried harvest and sickened livestock; the worst-hit district must be rebuilt.

fire.begin: Fire in Craft Row - a forge banked wrong, and the wind unkind.
during: The bucket line runs from the river; the Watch beats at the flames.
Smoke rolls over the square as the smiths' roofs go up.
Craft Row is a tunnel of heat; the Watch wets the next roof down and waits.
Somebody's apprentice runs back in for the tools and is dragged out again.
fire.pass: The fire is out. A row of workshops is char and cinder.
fire.cost: Buildings in one district burned down and rebuilt from nothing; the smiths sit idle until then.

drought.begin: No rain since the thaw. The river drops, and the wells go shy.
during: The crops stand yellow and brittle in the field.
The queue at the well starts before dawn.
The mill-wheel stands still in a riverbed of stones.
Dust comes off the fields in sheets and settles on the market bread.
drought.pass: Rain, at last. The river climbs, and Bellmire drinks easy again.
drought.cost: A harvest cut to nothing and thinning livestock; morale sinks until the wells fill.

famine.begin: The barns are near bare, and spring is a long way off.
during: Rations at the guild post; the thin get thinner.
A copper will not buy bread that is not there.
The guild post weighs every portion and still sends people away short.
Children are fed first, and the adults have agreed not to discuss it.
famine.pass: The first harvest comes in, and Bellmire eats again.
famine.cost: The town shrinks as the weak are lost; no growth until the barns refill.

sickness.begin: A fever walks the homes. The apothecary names it, then runs short of cures.
during: Doors chalked with a warning mark; the healers do not sleep.
The chapel bell tolls more than anyone likes.
The healers run out of simples before they run out of patients.
Market day is called off; the square has never looked bigger.
sickness.pass: The fever burns itself out. Bellmire counts its dead and opens the windows.
sickness.cost: The population falls, and a quarantine freezes trade and work while it lasts.

hurricane.begin: A great storm drives inland, and the sky turns the colour of a bruise.
during: Roofs peel away; the river bursts its low banks.
Nobody walks the wall in this.
The gate bar is doubled and the horses are brought inside the hall.
Something large goes past the window sideways and nobody goes to look.
hurricane.pass: The storm blows through. Bellmire is sodden and battered, but standing.
hurricane.cost: Roofs and buildings torn across the town, fields flooded, and days of repair.

tornado.begin: A finger of wind drops out of the storm and walks toward the town.
during: It takes a barn whole and sets it down in splinters.
Mind the sky - it has not lifted yet.
Carts are roped to posts and the posts are not reassuring.
It walks the far field twice and turns, and the whole town watches the turn.
tornado.pass: The wind lifts and is gone, leaving a straight scar of wreckage.
tornado.cost: A random line of buildings flattened, and livestock scattered or lost.

earthquake.begin: The ground rolls - the scar shudders, and so does everything above it.
during: Walls crack; the clapperless bell swings and almost rings.
Aftershocks, and nobody trusts a roof.
The well comes up muddy and the masons will not say why yet.
Every door in Bellmire sticks, and one wall leans that did not lean before.
earthquake.pass: The shaking stops. Bellmire checks its walls, and its dead.
earthquake.cost: Walls and buildings cracked or down town-wide; the scar may gape a little deeper.

meteor.begin: A star falls - too slow, too bright - and comes down past the fields.
during: The impact lights the night; the ground is scorched for a mile.
Something glitters in the new crater, and it hums like the scar.
Carters give the crater a wide berth; the horses refuse it outright.
The scar hums all night, as if something answered.
meteor.pass: The fires burn out. A crater smokes where the orchard used to stand.
meteor.cost: An outlying district or the orchard is destroyed - but the crater yields scarglass worth a fortune.

scarstorm.begin: The scar flares, and wild magic rolls up out of the dungeon mouth and over the town.
during: Every spell cast in Bellmire goes wrong; the lamps burn strange colours.
The livestock speak for a heartbeat, and the well runs uphill.
The apothecary corks everything and sits on the box.
A delver's lamp burns green, and the dark leans in to look.
scarstorm.pass: The scar quiets. The magic settles, mostly, and the town tallies what changed.
scarstorm.cost: Spellcasters are useless while it lasts; random buildings warp, and a few folk are scar-touched for good or ill.

flood.begin: The thaw comes all at once. The river climbs the banks, and keeps climbing.
during: The low district is ankle-deep, then knee-deep.
The Ford is gone under brown water; no crossing today.
The grain store is moved up a floor by every pair of hands in town.
Boats in the lane where carts should be, and someone fishing out of a window.
flood.pass: The water drops back, leaving mud in every doorway - but the town held.
flood.cost: Riverside buildings and stores ruined; the Ford and its trade shut until the river falls.

blight.begin: A black rot is in the grain - it came up in one field and did not stop there.
during: Whole rows are cut and burned before the rot can walk to the next field.
The miller turns away sack after sack, and says nothing, which is worse.
blight.pass: The blight burns out at the field edge. What is left of the harvest comes in early.
blight.cost: Most of the standing harvest is lost; food prices climb and the stores do not refill this season.

coldsnap.begin: The cold comes early and hard - the Ford freezes over in a night.
during: Firewood costs what wine cost last week, and the queue for it is longer.
The Watch walk in pairs now, because one man alone stops moving.
coldsnap.pass: The thaw comes. The Ford runs again, and Bellmire counts who it kept.
coldsnap.cost: Livestock lost and work stopped: building, trade and the fields all halt until the thaw.

events._note: Random world events (D33): bandit and monster camps that stand until cleared, and a wandering boss scaled to the town's level. Dead until wired.

bandit_camps.name: The Gallows Oak
bandit_camps.appears: Red Harl's lot have taken the west road. No caravan reaches the Ford unbled.
bandit_camps.while: Trade caravans are robbed; the market runs short and prices climb.
bandit_camps.cleared: Red Harl hangs from his own Gallows Oak. The west road is open again.

bandit_camps.name: The Mire Nest
bandit_camps.appears: Sedge the Toll holds the fen path and taxes everyone who is not her.
bandit_camps.while: Every trader by the fen pays Sedge first; the town's cut shrinks.
bandit_camps.cleared: Sedge the Toll pays her own toll at last. The fen path clears.

bandit_camps.name: The Burnt Mill
bandit_camps.appears: Cob Ashfoot's raiders have holed up in the burnt mill, firing a field a night to keep the town afraid.
bandit_camps.while: A field burns most nights; harvest and morale both drop.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Burnt Mill burns one last time. Cob Ashfoot runs, and keeps running.

bandit_camps.name: Scarside Camp
bandit_camps.appears: The Weasel's crew squat at the scar's edge, robbing the delvers who climb out.
bandit_camps.while: Returning delvers are waylaid; their gold and loot never reach Bellmire.
bandit_camps.cleared: Scarside Camp is cleared. Delvers come up to friends now, not knives.

monster_camps.name: The Bone Field
monster_camps.appears: Something below spat up its dead, and they are gathering in the north field.
monster_camps.while: The dead multiply nightly and gnaw at the outlying farms.
monster_camps.cleared: The Bone Field is put down. The north field is only a field again.

monster_camps.name: The Slime Warren
monster_camps.appears: A slime nest has taken the old quarry, and it doubles every night it is left alone.
monster_camps.while: The quarry is lost, and the nest creeps toward the homes.
monster_camps.cleared: The Slime Warren is burned out. The quarry stops twitching.

monster_camps.name: The Belltower Roost
monster_camps.appears: A roost of cave bats has taken the bell-tower; they foul the wells and spook every horse in town.
monster_camps.while: The wells need watching, and the beasts are restless while they hang there.
monster_camps.cleared: The Roost is cleared. The bell-tower is quiet. Almost.

wandering_boss.name: The Scarred Lord
wandering_boss.appears: A lord has climbed out of the scar and walks the open country - and it has grown to match the town it hunts.
wandering_boss.while: It razes an outlying farm each day it roams, and draws the dark along behind it.
wandering_boss.cleared: The wandering lord falls in the open field. Bellmire drags the body home as proof.
wandering_boss.note: Scales to the town's level: a lesser lord early, a greater lord once Bellmire is a city. Reuse the eight canon lords; never a new one.

growth_tiers._note: Town growth stages (D31/D32) - the town levels far too fast, so this is a long, earned climb. For each: the stage name, the crier's line on reaching it, and what a viewer should SEE appear. Complements town_levels_for_the_desktop (coarser, 7 levels). Dead until wired.

tiers.name: Crossing
tiers.crier: A handful of huts at a river crossing. Somebody calls it Bellmire.
tiers.see: Three or four huts, a cart, a cookfire.

tiers.name: Hamlet
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a hamlet now - a well dug, and a reason to stay.
tiers.see: A well, a few more homes, a fenced garden or two.

tiers.name: The Guild Post
tiers.crier: The guild plants a post at Bellmire. The post has a door, and the door is kept.
tiers.see: The guild post building, and the town's first lamp.

tiers.name: Village
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a village. The scar has a name, and so do we.
tiers.see: Homes clustered along a cart-track, chickens, a shared pen.

tiers.name: Market Day
tiers.crier: Market day comes to Bellmire. Measure the grain.
tiers.see: A market square with a few stalls, and the first outside traders.

tiers.name: The Chapel
tiers.crier: A chapel and a bell-tower rise. The bell has no clapper, and rings anyway.
tiers.see: The temple and its tower, and a small graveyard behind it.

tiers.name: Craft Row
tiers.crier: The smiths and masons raise Craft Row. Count the flasks.
tiers.see: Workshops trailing smoke, a forge-glow, the mill wheel turning.

tiers.name: The Garrison
tiers.crier: Bellmire raises a garrison. The guard has a yard now - and a Commander.
tiers.see: Barracks and a training yard, guards on patrol, E3PO up on the wall.

tiers.name: Market Town
tiers.crier: Bellmire stands as a proper market town. The caravans know the road.
tiers.see: A paved square, more districts, a busy Ford with its Ferryman.

tiers.name: The First Wall
tiers.crier: Stone goes up where the fields used to stop. Keep the door.
tiers.see: A low wall around the town's heart, and a gatehouse over the road.

tiers.name: Walled Town
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a walled town now. Let them come.
tiers.see: A full curtain wall, corner towers, a district banner on each quarter.

tiers.name: City in all but Charter
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a city in all but the charter - and the scar is deeper than it has ever been.
tiers.see: Dense districts, a second ring of homes outside the wall, traffic at every gate.
